antigens.rationale: Replace the long neutral amide side chain with alanine, removing contacted CG, CD, OE1 and NE2 while retaining CB. This tests side-chain contact removal at a geometrically implicated, solvent-accessible target position.
antigens.uncertainty: Existing WT contact union and reference exposure do not predict the substituted structure, interaction energetics, or biological outcome. Local structural effects remain unresolved.

antigens.rationale: Remove the aromatic ring, including the contacted CD2 and CE2 atoms, leaving an alanine methyl group. This provides an aromatic contact-reduction hypothesis distinct from the amide truncation at Q25. No specific interaction energy is inferred.
antigens.uncertainty: Existing WT contact union and reference exposure do not predict the substituted structure, interaction energetics, or biological outcome. Local structural effects remain unresolved.

antigens.rationale: Convert the terminal neutral amide to a carboxylate of similar side-chain reach. The contacted ND2/OD1 region is altered chemically; under ordinary near-neutral protonation assumptions this introduces negative charge.
antigens.uncertainty: Existing WT contact union and reference exposure do not predict the substituted structure, interaction energetics, or biological outcome. Local structural effects remain unresolved.

antigens.rationale: Convert the terminal carboxylate to a neutral amide while broadly retaining side-chain length. Contacted OE1/OE2 chemistry changes; under ordinary near-neutral protonation assumptions this removes negative charge.
antigens.uncertainty: Existing WT contact union and reference exposure do not predict the substituted structure, interaction energetics, or biological outcome. Local structural effects remain unresolved.

antigens.rationale: Remove the contacted phenolic OH while retaining the aromatic scaffold. This tests a localized polarity reduction with substantially less side-chain truncation than F14A.
antigens.uncertainty: Existing WT contact union and reference exposure do not predict the substituted structure, interaction energetics, or biological outcome. Local structural effects remain unresolved.

antigens.rationale: Add a methyl branch while retaining hydroxyl functionality at a position whose CB and OG occur in the contact union. This tests a modest size/branching change; the input does not establish a steric clash.
antigens.uncertainty: Existing WT contact union and reference exposure do not predict the substituted structure, interaction energetics, or biological outcome. Local structural effects remain unresolved.

antigens.rationale: Exact same Q-to-A transformation as Q25A: neutral amide side-chain truncation to methyl. Q38 is absent from both contact unions and has reference side-chain solvent exposure.
antigens.uncertainty: Chemistry is paired exactly, but local environment and reference exposure differ. Absence from the supplied WT union does not establish universal noninteraction or biological neutrality.

antigens.rationale: Exact same N-to-D transformation as N31D: amide-to-carboxylate exchange with similar reach. N42 is absent from both contact unions and has reference side-chain solvent exposure.

retention_policy.rule: Both metrics must meet or exceed their cutoff. Count each of WT, R27P, S30del, P34del and P33S once.
retention_policy.method: For each metric and engine: floor(100 × 0.90 × min(B5 WT, L10 WT)) / 100. Freeze these cutoffs; do not refit to incoming pairs.
retention_policy.interpretation: Provisional control-relative confidence screen, not a calibrated binding classifier. No labeled nonbinder set is available here to estimate specificity. The 90% allowance and rounding are policy choices, not an experimentally learned boundary. A failed cutoff is below-screen confidence, not proof of nonbinding. Retention is not the complement of the Red escape rule.
retention_policy.sensitivity_note: 85%, 90%, and 95% of the same WT-control anchors. Counts use available pairs; unknown pairs stay unknown. This is threshold sensitivity, not a statistical confidence interval.
